recipes.name: Beef Stroganoff with Steak
ingredients_raw: 1 pound sirloin steak, cut into bite size strips
1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed cream of mushroom soup

steps.text: Brown steak strips in a large skillet over medium-high heat; drain excess fat. Add onion and sauté for 5 minutes, or until tender. Stir in flour, salt, paprika, and ground black pepper.
Stir in soup; reduce heat to medium-low and simmer for 15 minutes. Stir in sour cream.
Prepare egg noodles according to package directions. Serve beef stroganoff over egg noodles.

raw_recipe.headline: Beef Stroganoff with Steak
raw_recipe.description: This creamy, tasty beef stroganoff is made with sirloin steak, mushroom soup, paprika, and nonfat sour cream for a lighter version of the traditional dish.

review.reviewBody: Excellent recipe! Tried it this evening. I prepared the beef last night (I bought & cubed 2 pieces of London Broil) & let it marinade in beef broth, garlic, seasoned salt, pepper and a decent merlot overnight because I knew I wouldn't be making this until today.) The only variation was I tweaked other member suggestions and added 2/3 cup beef broth and 1/3 cup water to cream of mushroom soup, added additional mushrooms and 1 cup of light cream. After simmering for 15 minutes, I added 1 cup sour cream (not fat free), dash of worstershire sauce, dash of nutmeg and parsley flakes. AWESOME results...not thick at all, very rich and creamy and totally delicious. Kinda fattening with this variation but so what...you can work it off in the gym tomorrow which is what I will do!!! Will definitely prepare again!

This was really tasty! I converted it to a slow cooker recipe. Browned the meat and onions, threw the mushroom soup mix along with the spices and a cup of red wine on the meat. Cooked for eight hours on low and added sour cream in the last half hour. No leftovers!

I've been making this for years. I have kids that don't like mushrooms so I add Lipton secrets mushroom-onion and a jar of mushroom gravy. It always taste better day after cuz it sits. So try to make early and cool it then warm for dinner.
Followed directions but used fresh mushrooms sautéed In butter and minced garlic with a dash of paprika.

My family loved this dish, even my picky meat eater. I do not particularly like sirloin steak, so I used two new york strip steaks, which were easy to cut thin strips. I cut the sour cream down to 1/2 cup, and added small amounts of milk until it thinned up a little. Otherwise it was too thick for noodles, as one other reviewer wrote. I added a good amount of garlic to add some flavor which saved the meal from blandness. Next time I will add baby bello mushrooms and maybe even a little tomato paste. YUM. Thanks for the recipe. Easy, and my kids love it. Definate keeper!

The seasoning for the meat in this is really tasty. I made this with a few additions/changes and the taste was outstanding. I marinated the meat for 2 hours beforehand with a little diced onion, some chili powder, Worcestershire sauce and oil. Then, I added a little chili powder to the meat seasoning and a splash of red wine when I was cooking. For the sauce, I added an addition can of soup (cream of chicken) and one block of Philly cream cheese. I also put in lots of sliced, fresh, white mushrooms. Family loved it. ^_^

I used some leftover steak instead of starting from raw meat, so that is definitely an option as it worked out just fine. Added a bit of olive oil to the pan to reheat the steak strips with then proceeded with the rest of the instructions. Upon adding the soup I felt it was a bit thick so I added some white wine to thin it out. Even our picky eater liked it!!! Will make this again!

I didn’t have time for the crock-pot version. This was quick, simple and delicious. I basically followed the recipe, the only things I added was, I sautéed a can of mushrooms along with some onions and garlic. I add a can of beef broth and a couple of dashes of Worcestershire sauce to the soup. Then I added 2 Tblsp of cream cheese along with the sour cream before serving. This was good. Daughter love it and Hubby asked me to make this again!!! Thanks for the recipe!

This recipe was super good. My husband absolutely loves beef stroganoff and so I decided to make this. The only thing I did different was I marinated my meat in soy sauce and minced garlic over night and to the sauce mixture I used about a half of can of beef broth. Without the beef broth the mixture was to thick for my liking. With these changes I will have to say PERFECTION!

I thought it was too thick when the condensed soup was added without water. Adding water and mixing that in was just what was needed. The flavor is good. My family liked the dish. It was simple to prepare. Excellent for my style of cooking, and my palette.

Came out great. I however did also have to alter the recipe. After cooking the beef and onions I deglazed the pot with a bit of water (would have used red wine if I had it) and then added the flour and spices. I used a can of Campbells Cream of Mushroom with Roasted Garlic soup instead and also added about 2 cups more of water (I didnt' want to use milk, felt like there was enough dairy) and added some Worschestershire sauce. Let that cook down and only added 3 big dollups of sour cream. Came out wonderful. Great color too - the garlic soup has some extra color and flavor to it. I also kept adding more paprika, but I love paprika!
Super easy to make. Added some Better Than Bullion beef base to the noodles and to the beef and gravy. Also added some garlic and worchester sauce for a little more flavor.
I loved it, did not change anything.
Added a little chicken broth and fresh garlic to it. My family loved it!!
Was good! … added Worcestershire sauce, red wine and sprinkle of garlic powder! Very tasty!
I used left over rib eye steak. I did add a half can of milk to the sauce and a splash of Worcestershire sauce. Easy dish, fit for company with a tossed salad and French bread. Yummy!
